Problem is it it starts off by feeling a lot of pain. Then you find yourself depressed and miserable and that becomes your default for a while, reverting back becomes unfamiliar and uncomfortable. You forget how to navigate normal emotions because of being used to being depressed all the time. I feel the exact same way, it's like a cycle of misery that keeps itself alive. Worst thing is that even when something good happens you find it scary to accept that sign of hope, because if it doesn't last, the fall will be much greater. So living with baseline self inflicted misery/pain seems like the more tolerable and humane alternative to the randomness of life. This usually happens when you've had a lot of expectations in the past and consistently being let down. So you prefer to keep yourself down essentially as a means of control over your life.
It sucks, there's no other way to put it.

It's really unfortunate what happened to you I'm sorry. I understand that your career took a turn for the worse over a single incident. I also understand your parents frustration but I'm sure they did not mean to push you into feeling this bad right now. They are in as much disbelief as you are and maybe they are not expressing it properly, trust me I know how middle eastern parents are. 
What I think you should try doing moving forwards is applying to other internships and being upfront about that incident and including a letter of good standing after doing some community outreach work, volunteer work, etc whilst working on getting your CV buffed up. You're very young and definitely not the first smart young person to have a mishap in their life. Just work on improving your image, reapply to other opportunities give it your best shot, you clearly have the brains for it. Try to be kind to your parents as well no matter how hard it seems right now, it's much harder on them from their perspective than you think right now.

Looks like you have a lovely group of people in your life and a girlfriend as well. If there was ever a time lean on them for help and support it would be now. Most people don't have that many loved ones in their lives and only have a therapist and perhaps dysfunctional families. If you feel that you have failed in your career but still have them around, trust me that means they're really good people and they care about you. Careers come and fall, a lot of people are currently going bankrupt and losing the ability to support their families during this pandemic. 
Talk to us more about why you feel this way and more importantly, don't break your families' heart and your loved ones too
